summary: Master PPP project preparation with feasibility, risk, and financing tools. Build bankable outputs and improve procurement readiness.
lede: Public-private partnership project preparation gives infrastructure and public investment professionals a structured way to assess project concepts before procurement. It covers project screening, feasibility and affordability checks, and risk allocation, with practical work on preparation documents such as screening memos, risk registers, and executive briefs. Participants also examine financial assumptions, governance, and procurement readiness to support decisions using available evidence and data.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already work with infrastructure projects, public investment decisions, procurement planning, or PPP transaction support and need to sharpen preparation quality.
prerequisites: Bring a laptop for spreadsheet review and document drafting. Participants should arrive with a working understanding of infrastructure delivery, project appraisal, or procurement workflows, plus a representative project case if available.
